study: Gitless fallback-scan boundary control for ignored-backup recovery
question: Does the selective-recovery gap observed with Git-aware .gitignore filtering disappear when agent-rollback uses its documented filesystem-walk fallback outside a Git repository?
environment_condition: The workspace contains the same .gitignore rule but no .git repository, so agent-rollback must use its documented filesystem-walk fallback.
contract: Both allowed build artifacts must be absent; every other project-file path and byte must equal the pre-command baseline.
arms: Native agent-rollback pre/post checkpoints, native operation-level revert, and replay of only the contract-allowed post-command state.
C-SDVR production project(base, observed, allowed) projection over the same pre-command and post-command byte maps.
pairing: For each file-count scale, both arms use identical baseline bytes and the same command-post byte map; exact byte-map equality is checked before recovery scoring.
primary_outcomes: backup paths present in the native checkpoint
limits: One public cleanup task family with three file-count scales; repeated scales are not independent tasks.
This is a negative control on scanner mode, not evidence of population-wide superiority.
The comparison is against the pinned agent-rollback commit and its documented filesystem-walk fallback.
